statements.t: Thereafter, the Company expects to have flexibility in how it allocates capital, including the potential return of capital to shareholders in the form of a buyback or dividend.

The Company continues to expect to reach a CPG revenue run rate of $40 million per year and positive consolidated net income on a run-rate basis by the end of 2027, based on doors secured to date and stores currently in its pipeline, and assuming completion of the Chubby transaction and the planned restructuring of its corporate overhead.
As we have said from the start, we look forward to closing with Chubby.
We expect it to substantially reduce our operating lease liabilities, allow us to eliminate our outstanding debt and add a guaranteed, secured receivable as an asset.

As the transition progresses, we will restructure our overhead and infrastructure around a much leaner CPG business, including a substantial reduction in our corporate workforce, and our senior management team will put its full time and capacity behind building it.

“Between the proceeds of the Chubby note and what we expect to be a very profitable CPG business, we believe GEN will have choices, including returning capital to shareholders — whether through a dividend or, if we feel our share price does not reflect the value of this business, share repurchases.

Company’s CPG business, including the risk that the Company does not achieve its anticipated revenue run rate, consolidated net income run rate or net margin on the anticipated timeline or at all; and the risk that the Company does not pay any dividend, repurchase any shares or otherwise return capital to shareholders.
